Walcott has catalogued from the Lower / Cambrian of North America alone, about one hundred / and sixty-five species of invertebrate animals belong- / ing to all of the six leading groups of these creatures. / In short, could we plunge our dredge into the Lower / Cambrian sea we should find examples of Trilobites / and other crustaceans of many kinds, constituting / indeed the majority of the inhabitants of the waters, / of all the different groups of Molluscan shell fishes, / of all allies of the modern star fishes, of coral animals / and their allies, of worms and of protozoa.
